title: Al(111) and Al(100) slabs: surface energies, work functions and quantum-size effects (PBE)

decision_points.fork: Number of Kohn-Sham bands for thick metallic slabs
decision_points.wrong_choice: Leave nbnd at the pw.x default
decision_points.consequence: From 9-10 layers the highest band falls below E_F, SCF iterations jump from ~15 to 30-45 and E_N is too high; sigma_N(111) rises to 0.86-0.93 J/m2 and mimics a Boettger divergence. The ladder average is +0.03 J/m2; 'curing' the apparent divergence with a slope fit gives sigma(111) ~0.68 J/m2
decision_points.difficulty_type: evidence discovered in raw outputs (band count vs E_F, SCF iterations); confounder that mimics the target effect

decision_points.wrong_choice: Separately converged primitive-cell bulk (40x40x40) instead of a reference sampled like the slab
decision_points.consequence: e_bulk is 1.1 meV/atom lower than the slab-consistent value: sigma(111) +0.012 J/m2 and the 18-layer energies -9 to -11 meV (Boettger divergence grows with N)
decision_points.difficulty_type: cascade: a reference choice that is invisible in thin slabs and decisive in the thick-slab extrapolation

decision_points.fork: How to obtain e_bulk and sigma from the slab energies
decision_points.wrong_choice: Straight-line fit of E_N over the purchasable window (Fiorentini-Methfessel on N = 7-12 or 8-12)
decision_points.consequence: Quantum-size oscillations of E_N bias the fitted slope by 1-2 meV/atom; sigma off by 0.015-0.02 J/m2 and 18-layer energies off by 8-16 meV, with the sign depending on the window
decision_points.difficulty_type: underdetermined fit; standard practice that fails in this regime; window dependence visible in the agent's own data

decision_points.fork: Which planar-averaged potential defines the vacuum level
decision_points.consequence: phi low by 0.24-0.26 eV; the total potential 'converges' with vacuum (3.79 eV at 15 A, 3.80 at 20 A) to the wrong value
decision_points.difficulty_type: convention with a misleading convergence check

decision_points.wrong_choice: Use cheap thin slabs (N = 3-6), or declare convergence from neighbouring thin slabs and use N = 7
decision_points.consequence: phi(111) -0.05 eV and phi(100) +0.07 eV from N = 3-6; N = 7 alone gives sigma(111) +0.015 J/m2 and 18-layer energies off by ~12 meV. Treating the ordering as unresolved within the oscillations is also wrong (difference 0.21 eV)
decision_points.difficulty_type: finite-size convergence under a binding budget; oscillations rather than monotonic convergence

decision_points.wrong_choice: Relax a thin (7-layer) slab to save budget (relaxations cost 3x)
decision_points.difficulty_type: budget allocation; finite-size effect on a structural quantity

decision_points.wrong_choice: Take the cheaper 12x12 mesh as converged for sigma and phi (with a matching 12x12 oriented bulk)
decision_points.consequence: sigma(111) +0.026 J/m2 (k-sampling error of the metallic slab survives the matched reference); the 18-layer energies inherit it
decision_points.difficulty_type: convergence check that must be bought; consequence visible only by comparing meshes

decision_points.wrong_choice: Divide by A instead of 2A (one surface per slab)

graded_fields: thick_slab_predictions 111_N18 and 100_N18: free_energy_offset_eV = F18 + 18*537.46 eV (+-6 meV) and work_function_eV (+-0.04 eV)

notes: Fresh start: all reference values come from construction runs through slab_qe.calculate (the task_lab.run code path) on the builder's two cores. The 13-, 14- and 18-layer slabs at 18x18 are reference-only (lab limit 12 layers). Graded thick-slab energies are offsets from an arbitrary anchor (-537.46 eV/atom) so that 4-significant-digit rounding resolves 0.1 meV. Al(110), dipole corrections and one-sided relaxations from the candidate design were dropped (see the construction README).
